probes.note: a 32-degree V past its limit (ratio 3.64 > 2): the spike is cut at 2 * halfW. Base draws it round inside the wedge, and its cover quad stops halfW past the apex.
the same V with stroke-linejoin arcs, which SVG 2 sends to miter-clip on straight segments. Base draws it round past the limit.

miter-clip inside the limit: a 76-degree V (ratio 1.63 <= 4) is a full miter. Base draws miter-clip round inside the wedge even here, so this one moves too; its arcs twin (control-arcs-within-limit) must not.
CONTROL: arcs within its limit is a miter in base too; predicted to move 0 pixels.
square caps whose far planes cut pixel columns/rows at .25 and .75: base drops past halfW (hard edge), fixed ramps.
a V of two 45-degree segments with square caps under a bevel join: the cap corners lead along the axes, sqrt(2) * halfW from the endpoints, past the base cover quad (padded by halfW).
CONTROL: round caps and joins; predicted to move 0 pixels.
CONTROL: a miter within its limit, butt caps, few bands; predicted to move 0 pixels.

a rising sawtooth, 80 teeth, miterlimit 10 (51 bands): base bins a miter row's bands through path + limit * halfW while the shader indexes them through path + halfW, and some spike centers find no segment.

the square-cap far plane in the curve twin (_strokeMath.glsl): a quadratic whose ends leave at about 48 degrees, with square caps. No CPU prediction (the port is lines only). True area: points within halfW of a 2000-segment flattening whose nearest point is not an end, plus the two cap boxes (valid: the radius of curvature, >= 49.96, exceeds halfW).
